reason: Replace and de-authorize Yance-owned production provider-gateway and physical model-routing infrastructure with mature OSS LiteLLM v1.95.0 base SDK Router/ComplexityRouter as the Model Brain production authority. Yance remains responsible only for product-specific task/context/privacy/capability projection, credential authority, queue/cancellation/stale-result fencing, signed execution evidence, user settings and final reply/send authority. LiteLLM must own provider normalization, streaming, retry/fallback, cooldown/load balancing, provider selection, token/cost normalization and physical model selection. LiteLLM may not be placed behind the legacy Yance router and no second Yance Model Gateway or Router is authorized.

digestCanonicalization.pathNormalization: Apply the repository normalizeChangedFiles contract: require exact repository-relative normalized paths, discard invalid paths, remove duplicates, then sort with JavaScript default Array.prototype.sort().
digestCanonicalization.canonicalText: Join the normalized sorted unique path list with LF and append exactly one trailing LF before hashing. This is the workPackageChangedFilesSha256 contract used by shared/release/implementationBranchPolicy.js.

liteLLM.integration: Adopt the exact MIT litellm/ source tree plus dependency versions/hashes from the exact upstream uv.lock. Use LiteLLM Router, tag filtering and ComplexityRouter directly as production gateway/routing authority; do not fork or copy the routing engine.

uv.role: Reuse the already-reviewed Yance build/sealing-time uv input; it must not be required at application runtime.

pythonBuildStandalone.role: Reuse the already-reviewed standalone CPython runtime supply-chain input for the sealed Windows Model Brain runtime.

routingOssFitDecision.productionAuthority: LiteLLM v1.95.0 base SDK Router + tag filtering + ComplexityRouter; AdaptiveRouter may be enabled only through the same pinned LiteLLM source when tests prove the configured policy.

routeLLM.reason: No official release/tag lifecycle and stale maintenance relative to current 2026 Model Brain production requirements. Mature OSS mandatory adoption does not require mechanically adopting an obsolete named upstream.

aurelioSemanticRouter.reason: Actively maintained and LiteLLM-compatible, but LiteLLM v1.95.0 already supplies the required complexity/adaptive/tag routing authority. Adding a second router would create unnecessary dependency and authority duplication.

vllmSemanticRouter.reason: Capable and active, but its local service/runtime model is materially heavier for native Windows/offline Yance P0 and is unnecessary while pinned LiteLLM already satisfies the routing contract.

openCoreBoundary.rootLicenseRule: enterprise/ is separately licensed; content outside enterprise/ is MIT under the pinned root LICENSE.
openCoreBoundary.nativeBridgePolicy: Do not compile or require the litellm-rust workspace for this P0. The pinned LiteLLM Python core has an official fallback when the optional _native bridge is absent; tests must prove the selected Router/provider paths work without it.
openCoreBoundary.dependencyMaterialization: Use the exact upstream uv.lock as dependency version/hash authority while excluding installation/emission of workspace projects and the root project, then place only the exact litellm/ Git tree into the sealed runtime. Runtime dependency resolution is forbidden.

yanceOwns: credential references and in-memory credential resolution

otherWorkPackageAuthoritiesUnchanged.LearningBrain: future Langfuse/DSPy/GEPA/eval/optimization authority; no implementation in this package

legacyRetirement.policy: Legacy Yance model routing/gateway code may remain physically present only when needed for compatible callers during P0, but it must be disconnected from all production inference decisions. No dual production authority is allowed.
mustLeaveProductionExecutionPath: aiGateway Yance cost-based physical model selection
mayRemainAsNonAuthoritativeFactsOrEviden: historical route records explicitly marked legacy/non-authoritative
legacyRetirement.deletionFollowUpAllowed: Dead legacy files may be physically deleted in this exact package only if already inside the authorized path set; otherwise deletion requires a separately authorized cleanup package. Their continued presence must not imply runtime authority.

runtimeBoundary.transport: private persistent child process over stdin/stdout NDJSON IPC; no second HTTP Model Gateway
runtimeBoundary.childOwns: pinned LiteLLM Router instances and provider calls only
runtimeBoundary.credentialFlow: Yance security credential authority -> in-memory Model Brain projection -> child process request/environment for the invocation; never renderer/persistent plaintext/logs
runtimeBoundary.runtimeMissingBehavior: Model inference fails closed with explicit Model Brain unavailable/degraded state; legacy Yance provider clients must never be used as fallback.
runtimeBoundary.wp7Packaging: Out of scope for this core P0. If the existing WP7 trusted product assembler requires new shared-path integration for the sealed Model Brain runtime, create a separate exact-path packaging closure after this core runtime is GREEN.

yanceMayProjectHardRequirements: simple reply vs deep relationship reasoning
routingSignals.projectionMechanism: logical model group plus LiteLLM deployment tags/metadata and request metadata; Yance must not score/rank physical providers after projection.
routingSignals.historicalQualityFutureInput: Reserve structured route/model/usage/cost/result identifiers so later Langfuse quality evidence can feed the same mature routing authority without changing the gateway contract. Do not implement Langfuse in this package.

mandatoryFailureFirstContracts: The first implementation commit contains tests only. Before product code, those tests must produce a causal RED because the pinned LiteLLM runtime/integration is absent and legacy Yance routing/direct-provider execution is still authoritative.

No production inference may select champion, primary, fallback, emergency, provider or model in Yance before entering LiteLLM. Physical model/provider selection must be proven to originate from the pinned LiteLLM Router result.

Production aiGateway execution must not call legacy aiQualityRouteAuthority.routePlan/classifyFailure, workload placement, provider failure-domain, Yance budget routing or model service task-routing authorities to choose/retry/fallback a physical model.
modelExecutor must not perform a direct provider switch to ollamaClient/openAiCompatibleClient for model inference; qualification and benchmark calls must traverse LiteLLM too.
mediaIntelligenceService image/video representative-frame model inference must traverse Model Brain/LiteLLM and must not call ollamaClient directly.
bilingualUnderstandingService must not call aiGateway.resolveRoute to preselect a translation model; translation must use the logical group/tags path into LiteLLM.
modelAutoActivationService and modelRegistry qualification/benchmark flows must not auto-write or rebalance authoritative primary/fallback physical routes.
No usable sealed Model Brain runtime is an explicit fail-closed/degraded RED for AI inference; legacy direct provider clients must never become fallback authority.
LiteLLM tag filtering must fail closed when mandatory privacy/modality/native-register capability tags have no eligible deployment.

The pinned LiteLLM ComplexityRouter must be the complexity-tier classifier/routing implementation when complexity routing is enabled; no copied or rewritten Yance complexity scoring engine is allowed.
Provider retry/fallback/cooldown/load balancing/rate-limit handling must be performed by LiteLLM rather than duplicate Yance loops.

Successful result evidence must bind the selected physical model to LiteLLM model_id/result metadata and bind token/cost metrics to LiteLLM/provider-normalized result data; Yance catalog cost estimation must not be production cost authority.

The shipped runtime contains only the pinned MIT litellm/ upstream source tree and the dependency closure required for the base SDK path; enterprise/ and litellm-proxy-extras/ source/distributions/modules are absent.
The runtime must not require LiteLLM Proxy Server, litellm[proxy], litellm-enterprise, a Rust toolchain, pip, uv, Git, system Python or online dependency resolution at application startup.
Credential plaintext must not be persisted, logged, exposed to renderer state, included in route receipts, or copied into SBOM/provenance artifacts.

Windows x64 sealed runtime must be built from the exact pinned upstream/source/lock/tool/runtime inputs and pass offline import, Router construction, tag-routing, complexity-routing and health closure with build tools absent from the shipped runtime.
Deterministic CycloneDX 1.7 runtime SBOM plus upstream provenance/license/tree evidence must be generated and verified before GREEN.
Letta, Graphiti, Parlant, Persona, Learning Brain, Voice, Facebook and Presence authorities remain unchanged and are not implemented or modified by this work package.
The final implementation changed-path set must remain within the exact 20 authorized paths and retain SHA-256 19e51c52a1247c95b45ec1beb13bfb3f998694498429a182e96d02287bef16f2.
Independent exact-Head review must have zero unresolved P0/P1 findings before the implementation can reach the final merge boundary.
